flavor_text.one_line: A measured faith of ledgers and tombs, where wealth matters because memory must be maintained.
flavor_text.one_paragraph: The Gilded Memory teaches that wealth is a trust rather than a sin or glory, useful only when properly recorded, inherited, and spent to strengthen the chain between living clan and honored dead. Its priests arbitrate debts, preserve vault genealogies, and bless trade so long as bargains do not poison communal memory. Extremes of law or chaos are regarded as costly imbalances best corrected before they become ruin.
flavor_text.creation_myth_summary: Azrumek counted the first stones, named their worth, and raised the first ancestor vault so the dead could remember what the living would otherwise squander.
flavor_text.moral_code_summary: Keep exact records, enrich family without despoiling the clan, honor the dead with maintenance and gifts, and avoid zeal that turns fairness into tyranny or anarchy.
